findings.message: Doc comments in packages/simulation/src/duel/state.ts are off by one against the code. Bolt.life (line 47) and Zone.life (line 61) say "Frames it still exists after the current one", but the count includes the current state. A released bolt is stored with life = projectile.life (90). sweepBolts (step.ts:337) and nextZone (step.ts:378) drop the entity when a state holding life 1 is stepped, so a state with life 1 is the entity's last. That gives 90 bolt states and 180 screen states, which ember.test.ts 'dies at the end of its life' and smoke.test.ts 'expires on time' both assert. schema.ts ('the one it appears on included') and docs/fruit-kits.md ('this one included') describe it correctly. Only comments are wrong, not behaviour, but a renderer or netcode author reading state.ts would be off by one frame.
